title: Observed preflight silently accepts non-mapping bundle entries
suggestion: Reject when any top-level patch item is not a record, and replace the test that codifies silent filtering with an observed-preflight rejection assertion.
rationale: loadPatchLayer verifies only that the YAML root is an array and then drops every non-record item with filter(isRecord). An installed bundle containing a valid entry plus a scalar therefore reaches observed preflight as a reduced patch and can return accepted:true; the existing test at commands.spec.ts:3399-3425 explicitly expects this fail-open result. This contradicts the documented requirement that every effective top-level row be structurally valid and means preflight can approve input that was not fully reviewed.

title: Artifact paths can escape the package directory on Windows or through symlinks
suggestion: Reject path.isAbsolute(relativePath) on the host platform and resolve the candidate path through realpath before verifying it remains under realpath(packageDir) with a separator-aware containment check.
rationale: The lexical check rejects only leading slash, dot-dot segments, and NUL. On Windows it accepts drive-absolute and UNC paths, and on every platform it accepts a package-local symlink whose target is outside packageDir. inspectResolvedArtifact then reads the resulting bundle patch or accepts the resulting main file as candidate-owned evidence, so an untrusted artifact can make static admission inspect or approve files outside its package.

title: The advertised smoke deadline does not bound synchronous artifact inspection
suggestion: Move installed-artifact inspection into a cancellable child process governed by the remaining deadline, or narrow the documented guarantee to the child stages and enforce input size and filesystem constraints separately.
rationale: inspectInstalledSmokeProfile performs synchronous manifest, lockfile, patch, and filesystem reads before the next deadline check. If those reads block on a slow/network filesystem or consume excessive time on oversized input, the command can exceed 55 seconds and only report a timeout after inspection returns. The Promise.resolve deadline check cannot interrupt the synchronous work, so the documented single wall-clock bound is not enforced.
